archetypes.name: line-ref-accuracy
archetypes.rationale: The plan anchors every implementation step to specific line numbers in the scope files; if any cited line is off the implementation will target wrong code, silently breaking the carryover guard.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan cites specific line numbers throughout: review-and-fix.sh lines 1162, 273, 1300, 1510; review-implement-step5-loop.sh lines 339-341, 398, 408; test-review-and-fix.sh lines 494-531, 533-563. Read each file at those lines and verify that the code described in the plan is actually present at those locations — check that the described variable names, function names, and behavior match. Also verify that the plan's claim that review-implement-step5-loop.sh sources review-and-fix.sh at line 3 (making pre_coder_snapshot_dir available) is accurate. Flag any discrepancy between the plan's description of a line and its actual content, since a wrong anchor causes the implementer to modify or read the wrong location. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: grant-boundary-check
archetypes.rationale: The entire relocation strategy's security value depends on the Codex and Cursor coder dispatch flags being exactly what the plan asserts; if the actual grants differ the sibling dir is not protected.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan's security model rests on two assertions: that Codex is granted write access only to its -C (repo root) and --add-dir round_dir flags, and that Cursor is limited to --workspace "$PWD" and therefore never reached round_dir. Locate the actual Codex and Cursor coder dispatch invocations in the repository (search lib-codex-launcher-common.sh, lib-cursor-launcher-common.sh, launch-codex-implement.sh, launch-cursor-implement.sh, or run-external-agent.sh) and verify the exact --add-dir, -C, and --workspace flags passed to each coder match what the plan assumes. Check whether $IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR itself could fall inside a broader grant (e.g. if the repo root and IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR share a common ancestor that is granted), which would make the sibling dir still reachable despite the relocation. Flag any mismatch between the plan's stated grant boundaries and the actual dispatch code. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: artifact-reference-sweep
archetypes.rationale: The plan identifies exactly two scripts as all readers/writers of the snapshot artifacts, but any undiscovered third caller left reading the old round_dir path would silently produce split-brain state after relocation.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan names only review-and-fix.sh and review-implement-step5-loop.sh as scripts that read or write pre-coder-head.txt, pre-coder-tracked-paths.txt, and pre-coder-path-diffs/. Search the broader codebase — including other scripts under skills/, root scripts/, hooks/, and .claude/skills/ — for any references to these artifact names or to the pre-coder-path-diffs directory literal. Also check whether any .md documentation files (including the sibling .md contract files) describe the old round_dir/pre-coder-* path layout in a way that would become stale and misleading after relocation. If any undiscovered caller exists or any doc continues to describe the old path as authoritative, the plan's scope is incomplete. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
